claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr undergoes rapid oxygen penetration in high-temperature oxidizing environments.
High-temperature oxygen penetration degrades the mechanical properties of untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Pack cementation aluminization introduces aluminum into the surface layers of cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Subsequent high-temperature oxidation of the aluminized alloy forms a continuous Al2O3 scale.
The Al2O3 scale formed on aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will be thin and adherent.
The alumina scale will be stable and slow-growing during high-temperature oxidation.
The alumina scale acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Restricting oxygen diffusion through the alumina scale limits oxidation of the underlying HfNbTaTiZr substrate.
Aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit significantly lower oxygen uptake than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr at approximately 1000 °C in air for approximately 100 hours.
Aluminization will improve the oxidation resistance of HfNbTaTiZr at approximately 1000 °C in air for approximately 100 hours.
Aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will retain the untreated alloy's baseline room-temperature tensile ductility after the specified exposure.
Aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will retain the untreated alloy's baseline yield strength at 1000 °C under strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Poor coating adhesion or nonoptimal coating thickness may compromise the intervention's effectiveness.
